summary:
**Earth Jukebox — Hear Our Planet. Understand Our Future**

Earth Jukebox is an interactive web application developed by Team Stellar Sparks for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026. It transforms Earth's changing scientific data into sound, helping people explore our planet through both visual and audio experiences.

The platform features interactive themes including global temperature, carbon dioxide, ocean heat, vegetation, and natural events. Users can explore data, move through time, and listen as scientific measurements are translated into sound using carefully designed musical mappings. It also provides plain-language explanations, data provenance, scientific limitations, and accessible controls.

Earth Jukebox addresses the challenge by making Earth information more engaging, understandable, and accessible, including for visually impaired users. It is important because it offers a new way to experience environmental changes, encourages curiosity about Earth science, and helps people connect with the data behind our planet's changing conditions.

**Live Demo:** https://earth-jukebox-three.vercel.app/
details:
Project Details: Earth Jukebox — Hear Our Planet. Understand Our Future.

Team: Stellar Sparks

1. What does the project do, and how does it work?

Earth Jukebox is an interactive, browser-based application that transforms Earth's changing environmental data into sound. It allows users to explore five themes: global temperature, carbon dioxide, ocean heat, vegetation, and natural events.

Users can select a theme, explore its available data, move through time, and listen as measurements are converted into sound using documented sonification mappings. For example, in the temperature theme, warmer years produce higher and brighter sounds, while cooler years produce lower and softer sounds.

The project also includes a NASA visual sonification feature. Users can select prepared NASA images and video scores, explore their brightness patterns, and listen to their audio representations. Playback controls include play, pause, stop, replay, looping, volume adjustment, and mute.

2. What benefits does it have?

  • Makes complex Earth science information more engaging and easier to explore.
  • Provides an alternative way to experience data beyond traditional charts and graphs.
  • Supports accessibility through keyboard-operable controls, screen-reader readouts, text alternatives, reduced-motion support, and adjustable audio.
  • Explains data sources, units, mappings, and limitations to help users understand what the sounds represent.
  • Encourages students, educators, and the public to become more interested in Earth science and environmental awareness.

3. What is the intended impact?

Our goal is to help people develop a stronger connection with our planet by allowing them to hear patterns in Earth's changing systems. We want to make scientific information more inclusive, interactive, and memorable, especially for people who may find traditional visual representations difficult to access.

We hope Earth Jukebox can inspire curiosity about climate change, environmental monitoring, and the importance of understanding our planet through scientific data.

4. What tools and technologies did we use?

We developed Earth Jukebox as a browser-based application using:

  • HTML, CSS, and JavaScript ES modules for the web interface and application functionality.
  • Web Audio API for generating and controlling sound.
  • SVG charts for interactive data visualization.
  • NASA images and videos for prepared visual sonification scores.
  • Scientific datasets and published Earth-science records for environmental data exploration.
  • Vercel for hosting and publicly deploying the application.

The application uses prepared brightness samples from selected NASA media. These represent rendered pixel brightness, not the underlying scientific measurements. The project clearly distinguishes these artistic sound representations from actual natural recordings or direct NASA measurements.

5. How is the project creative?

The creative idea behind Earth Jukebox is to make Earth science something people can not only see and read, but also hear. We combine scientific information, music-inspired sound design, interactive visualization, and accessible web technology.

Instead of simply displaying environmental changes as numbers or graphs, we translate patterns into sound, creating a more immersive way to explore our planet. This combination of science and sound makes the project a creative interpretation of the Earth Information Jukebox challenge.

6. What factors did our team consider?

While developing the project, we considered:

  • Scientific accuracy: Clearly identifying data sources, units, and limitations.
  • Accessibility: Supporting different ways of interacting with and understanding information.
  • User experience: Keeping navigation and audio controls simple and intuitive.
  • Transparency: Explaining how data is translated into sound and distinguishing observations from demonstration data.
  • Performance: Using prepared, compact visual scores so large video files do not need to load in the browser.
  • Responsible communication: Making clear that sonification is a designed representation, not a natural recording of Earth.

Earth Jukebox is our attempt to bring science and creativity together and help everyone experience the changing story of our planet in a new way.

Live Project: https://earth-jukebox-three.vercel.app/
